`case_study:karvy-2019` | 2019-11-22 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Karvy Stock Broking (unlisted, one of India's largest retail brokers) used clients' power-of-attorney to pledge their securities (reported ~Rs 2,300-2,700 cr of client shares, >95,000 clients) with banks/NBFCs for its own loans; a net ~Rs 1,096 cr moved to group company Karvy Realty between Apr 2016 and Oct 2019. NSE's inspection led to a SEBI ex-parte order on 22 Nov 2019 barring new clients; NSDL transferred shares back to ~80,000+ clients; SEBI refused relief to lenders who had taken the pledges. NSE expelled Karvy in 2020 and SEBI later cancelled its registration; the CMD was arrested in 2021. Visible flags: (1) a broker borrowing heavily from banks against 'own' securities that were actually client holdings; (2) group diversion into real estate; (3) mismatch between client ledger balances and demat holdings (only detectable by regulators/clients via CAS). Investor-level signal: securities in your Consolidated Account Statement moving to the broker's pool account or being pledged without your consent. Outcome: SEBI tightened norms (margin pledge/re-pledge system in 2020, curbs on PoA, segregation and client-fund reporting). Lesson: custody/counterparty risk is part of portfolio risk -- reconcile the monthly CAS, avoid giving open PoA, spread holdings across brokers.

**Lesson:** Reconcile CAS monthly; custody risk is real
**Spotted early by:** NSE inspection
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:avoid-ruin`
**Sources:** <https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/dec-2019/1576257310795.pdf> ; <https://www.moneylife.in/article/karvy-stock-broking-pledged-client-securities-diverted-funds-to-group-companies-sebi-cancels-ksbls-registration/70963.html> ; <https://www.bloombergquint.com/law-and-policy/sebi-bars-karvy-stock-broking-from-taking-new-clients-2>

`case_study:eli-lilly-2018-2025` · tickers US-LLY · confidence: verified

Lilly was a mid-sized pharma (~$80-110 in 2018 [unverified]) behind J&J, Pfizer, Merck. Tirzepatide (dual GIP/GLP-1): SURPASS-2 (2021) beat semaglutide in diabetes; SURMOUNT-1 (Apr 2022) showed ~21-22% weight loss; Mounjaro approved May 2022, Zepbound (obesity) Nov 2023. 2024 sales: Mounjaro $11.5bn, Zepbound $4.9bn; Q3 2025 Mounjaro $6.5bn (+109%), Zepbound $3.6bn (+185%). Lilly took ~63% of US branded obesity scripts by Q3 2025 and invested tens of billions in manufacturing capacity. Nov 21 2025: first drugmaker to a $1tn market value (~$1,050+/share [unverified]) — ~10-13x from 2018; +75% since Zepbound launch vs S&P +50%; ~50x forward earnings. Split: EPS grew several-fold 2022-25 but P/E also expanded from ~20x to ~50x [approx]. Drawdown: ~-30%+ between Aug 2024 high and mid-2025 on oral-pill data and pricing worries [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2021-22: head-to-head data beating the market leader's molecule (SURPASS-2), then SURMOUNT-1's weight-loss magnitude — public, peer-reviewed, before revenue. Who caught it: broad healthcare growth funds; no single documented investor found. Risks: price cuts under US government deals, orforglipron/oral competition, Novo/new entrants. LESSON: in category creation the winner is often the best-data fast follower with manufacturing scale, not the pioneer; head-to-head trial data is the early public signal.

- **Start → end:** ~$80-110 (2018) [unverified] → ~$1,050+ ($1tn cap, Nov 21 2025) [unverified per-share] (~10-13x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** EPS several-fold + P/E ~20x->~50x
- **Max drawdown:** ~-30%+ (2024-25) [unverified]
- **Early signal:** SURPASS-2 head-to-head win 2021; SURMOUNT-1 2022
- **Who caught it:** not documented
- **Ended/stalled:** not ended as of Nov 2025
- **Lesson:** best-data fast follower + capacity wins the category
- **Sources:** [1](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/lilly-becomes-first-drugmaker-join-145237391.html) · [2](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/eli-lilly-1-trillion-pharmaceutical-market-value-obesity-alzheimers/721819/) · [3](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/economics/2025/11/21/lilly-becomes-first-drugmaker-to-hit-us1-trillion-valuation-on-weight-loss-demand/) · [4](https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2794582/lilly-crosses-1-trillion-market-cap-here-s-what-is-driving-the-rally)

body:
- **IT measures in `score.py`** (matched on the metric text, after the bank measures and before the segment filter):
  | Measure | Phrases it catches | Scored from |
  |---|---|---|
  | `cc_revenue_growth_yoy_pct`, `cc_revenue_qoq_pct` | "constant currency", "CC growth", "CC QoQ / sequential" | `--csv` only (company-reported) |
  | `usd_revenue_growth_yoy_pct`, `usd_revenue_qoq_pct` | "revenue in USD", "dollar growth", "USD QoQ" | `--csv` only |
  | `ebit_margin_pct` | "EBIT margin", "EBIT band", "operating band" (not EBITDA) | `--csv` (company EBIT governs), else screener (OP − depreciation) / sales |
  | `tcv_usd_mn` | "TCV", "total contract value", "deal wins", "large deals", "bookings", "ACV" | `--csv` (FY = sum of quarters) |
  | `utilisation_pct`, `attrition_pct` (lower is better), `headcount` | "utilisation" (not plant/capacity utilisation), "attrition", "headcount" | `--csv` only |
  | `top5_client_share_pct`, `top10_client_share_pct` (lower is better) | "top 5 / top 10 clients" | `--csv` only |
  - Growth measures use the growth thresholds, margins and people ratios use the 0.3 / 1.5 pp thresholds, and TCV and headcount use the 95% / 80% ratio thresholds.
  - Vertical, geography or client-level CC growth, "organic" or "ex-acquisition" variants, CAGRs and segment EBIT are **blocked**: they return *not-auto-scorable* rather than falling through to INR revenue growth or screener OPM. In v1.1, "EBIT margin 14-16%" was read as EBITDA margin (screener OPM runs about 3 pp higher for IT). "CC growth 10%" was read as INR revenue growth, which can be off by 2-4 pp of FX.
  - **Company EBIT and EBITDA differ from screener for most IT firms** (IT_MIDCAPS_peer_comparison.md, section 3.4). Supply a CSV row `ebit_margin_pct` whenever the company figure is known.
- **`parse_target`:** "USD 500 mn", "$1.5 bn", "$300-350 million" and "$500 mn+" become USD mn (with a floor for "+"). "Double-digit" means ≥10%, "low double-digit" 10-12% and "high single-digit" 7-9%. Previously these returned nothing.
- **`candidates.py` categories:** `deal_wins` (TCV, ACV, large/mega deals, bookings, executable order book; placed before `order_book`/`order_inflow` only for these words). `people` (attrition, utilisation, headcount, freshers, wage hikes). `client_concentration` (top-N clients, $X mn+ client buckets). "Constant currency" and "CC" also count toward `revenue_growth`, and "EBIT band" toward `margin`. The memdb category map (`scripts_it_peers/build_seed.py`) puts the three new categories in the "other" group.
- **Regression check:** all 363 promises in the existing `memdb/seeds/*promises*.json` give the same `infer_measure` and `parse_target` result as v1.1. Plant-capacity "utilisation" (SKIPPER, ENDURANCE) is deliberately excluded from `utilisation_pct`.
- **Data access notes:**
  - Coforge's NSE transcript filings are one-page cover letters with a link. Download the PDFs from `investors.coforge.com/quarter-reports` and pass them with `--local`. Its results, press releases and factsheets *are* on NSE.
  - Persistent's Q4FY26 filing is a cover letter (`persistent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Analyst-Call-Transcript-Q4FY26.pdf`), and Persistent held no Q1FY27 call.
  - `turns.py` needs `--roster` for Persistent and cannot split Mphasis's layout. For Mphasis, read the raw text.
  - `fetch.py` dated Mphasis's Q1FY26 call 2025-07-01; the correct date is 25-Jul-2025.
